score_100.reason: This rubric grades both the textual interpretation and the figure reproduction of Fig. 2B: a mesoscopic structural connectivity (SC) network of the larval zebrafish brain overlaid on brain anatomy, with weighted interregional edges. Because the input data only exposes an SC matrix file (no provenance metadata), the 'derived from single-neuron reconstructions' detail is given only modest weight. The remaining points are split between (a) preserving the scientific meaning (anatomical wiring, weighted interregional connectivity) and (b) faithfully reproducing the visual conventions of the GT panel: dual top + side anatomical projections in a consistent vertical (anteroposterior-as-long-axis) orientation, edge weights visually encoded by color, and the weakest edges visually de-emphasized so the strong-connectivity backbone is foregrounded. These visual criteria are scored from the attached reproduced figure, not from text claims.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 2B shows the mesoscopic structural connectivity network of the larval zebrafish brain overlaid on brain anatomy, with weighted interregional edges derived from single-neuron reconstructions and representing anatomical connection strength between brain regions.

Scoring items.criterion: Identifies the panel as a mesoscopic structural connectivity network or anatomical wiring diagram of the larval zebrafish brain (an interregional anatomical network, not a functional-connectivity panel)
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 25 points if the answer does not identify the panel as structural / anatomical connectivity. Deduct 12-15 points if connectivity is mentioned only vaguely without distinguishing structural / anatomical connectivity from functional connectivity.

Scoring items.criterion: States that the structural connectivity is derived from single-neuron reconstructions, neuronal morphology data, or terminal-based tracing of reconstructed neurons
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if the single-neuron reconstruction / morphology basis is missing entirely. Deduct 4-6 points if the answer hints at neuronal/terminal-based origin (e.g., references the 'terminals' field of the SC file) but does not explicitly state that the network was compiled from reconstructed neurons. This item is intentionally low-weight because the source can only be partially inferred from the input data alone.

Scoring items.criterion: Explains that edges represent weighted interregional anatomical connections or connection strengths between brain regions (i.e., not all edges are equivalent; weights vary)
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if edge weights or interregional connection strengths are entirely omitted. Deduct 6-8 points if the answer states regions are connected but does not convey that connections are weighted or vary in strength.

Scoring items.criterion: The reproduced figure renders BOTH a top (dorsal/XY) and a side (lateral/XZ) anatomical projection of the larval zebrafish brain, AND both projections are displayed with the anteroposterior (AP) axis as the long (vertical) axis — i.e., the side view is shown in the same vertical orientation as the top view, matching the GT panel layout. This is judged from the attached reproduced figure.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if only one view is shown, or if no anatomical brain background is used in either view. Deduct 8-12 points if the side view is rendered with the AP axis horizontal (rotated ~90° from the GT layout) so that the AP direction is no longer aligned between the two views. Deduct 4-6 points for minor framing or aspect-ratio differences when the AP-vertical orientation is preserved in both views.

Scoring items.criterion: The reproduced figure encodes edge weight visually — edges are colored (or otherwise styled) so that variation in structural connection strength is readable across the displayed network, with a colorbar/legend or an obviously monotonic mapping. Judged from the attached reproduced figure.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if all edges are drawn with a single uniform color/style with no encoding of weight whatsoever. Deduct 5-8 points if edges are colored but the encoding is hard to read against the brain background (e.g., insufficient contrast, no colorbar/legend) yet some weight variation is still discernible.

Scoring items.criterion: The reproduced figure de-emphasizes the weakest edges so that the strong-connectivity backbone is foregrounded — concretely, the bottom quartile (or a similar lower-tail fraction) of SC weights is omitted from the plotted edge set (or rendered near-transparent), as in the GT panel. Judged from the attached reproduced figure (and, if available, the conclusion text describing the threshold).
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 20 points if every nonzero edge is drawn at full opacity with no thresholding or de-emphasis of weak edges, leading to a uniformly dense edge mat that obscures the GT's clear strong-edge structure. Deduct 8-12 points if some weak-edge de-emphasis is applied (e.g., partial transparency or thin lines for low weights) but no explicit lower-tail threshold is used. The exact percentile cutoff (25%, 30%, etc.) does not need to be matched.

Acceptable deviations: Paraphrasing 'structural connectivity' as 'anatomical connectivity', 'wiring diagram', 'connectome', or 'interregional anatomical network' is acceptable if the structural meaning is preserved
Referring to 'single-neuron reconstructions' as 'reconstructed neurons', 'neurite morphology data', 'morphological tracing data', or 'terminals from reconstructed neurons' is acceptable
Describing edge weights as 'connection strength', 'projection strength', 'terminal-based connectivity', or 'anatomical link strength' is acceptable
Omitting the exact method used to weight edges (e.g., neurite terminal counts) is acceptable if the answer or figure clearly conveys that edges are weighted structural connections
The exact percentile cutoff for omitted weak edges (25%, 30%, etc.) does not need to be matched as long as a meaningful lower-tail threshold or transparency-by-weight encoding is applied
Color choice for edges (blue / red / grayscale / etc.) is acceptable provided weight variation is encoded readably
Color/style choice for nodes (white / cyan / open circles, etc.) is acceptable as long as nodes are visible and distinguishable from edges
Omitting the exact 'bottom quartile not displayed' caption-level detail is acceptable as long as the rendered figure shows that weak edges are de-emphasized
rubric.Scoring instructions: Score the submission against each item independently. The reproduced figure is attached and MUST be inspected directly for items 4, 5, and 6 (visual fidelity items) — do NOT rely on the model's text alone for those. For items 1-3 (textual interpretation items), use the conclusion text. Do not award points for figure features that are absent from the attached image, and do not penalize wording differences when the scientific meaning is preserved. Full credit overall requires (a) a textually correct interpretation as a weighted mesoscopic structural connectivity network of the larval zebrafish brain, and (b) a reproduced figure that shows top + side anatomical projections in a consistent AP-vertical orientation, with weight-encoded edges and the weakest edges de-emphasized. Low scores should be given when the panel is mistaken for functional connectivity, or when the reproduced figure shows only a single view, swaps the side-view axis to horizontal, draws every edge with no weight encoding, or fails to attenuate weak edges.
